title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 73 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 452–454 (Night 73, continuing directly from nights-72), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 73 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The eunuch, sent a second time to find the unseen singer, comes upon the stoker, who denies it and pleads that he is a stranger; Ḍawʾ al-Makān, woken and warned, cries out a third time in verse on love of the homeland, and the servant, hidden behind them, steps forward and greets him. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.l: And when it was the night, the third and the seventy,
sentences.i: And when it was the seventy-third night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ نُزْهَةَالزَّمَانِ أَرْسَلَتِ الْخَادِمَ يُفَتِّشُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna nuzhata al-zamāni arsalati al-khādima yufattishu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Nuzhat al-Zamān sent the servant, searching for him,
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Nuzhat al-Zamān sent the servant to search for him,
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”) and joins نزهة to الزمان; both are read as separate words.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تَرْجِعَ لِي وَتَقُولَ مَا وَجَدْتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu iyyāka an tarjiʿa lī wa-taqūla mā wajadtuhu
sentences.l: and said to him: Beware that you return to me and say: I did not find him.
sentences.i: and told him: Do not dare come back to me and say you could not find him.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ الْخَادِمُ يَضْرِبُ فِى النَّاسِ وَيَدُوسُ فِى الْخِيَمِ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ أَحَدًا مُسْتَيْقِظًا وَجَمِيعُ النَّاسِ مِنَ التَّعَبِ نَائِمُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja al-khādimu yaḍribu fī al-nāsi wa-yadūsu fī al-khiyami fa-lam yajid aḥadan mustayqiẓan wa-jamīʿu al-nāsi mina al-taʿabi nāʾimūna
sentences.l: So the servant went out, striking among the people and treading in the tents, and did not find anyone awake, the whole of the people sleeping from weariness.
sentences.i: So the servant went out, pushing through the crowd and trampling among the tents, but found no one awake; everyone was asleep from exhaustion.
sentences.n: The print writes فى with a dotless ى; the spelling is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَجَأَ إِلَى الْوَقَّادِ فَوَجَدَهُ قَاعِدًا مَكْشُوفَ الرَّأْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-jaʾa ilā al-waqqādi fa-wajadahu qāʿidan makshūfa al-raʾsi
sentences.l: Then he came to the stoker and found him sitting, bare-headed.
sentences.i: Then he came to the stoker and found him sitting there bare-headed.
sentences.n: The print has فجأ, evidently for فجاء “he came”; it is read so, with the hamza as printed.

sentences.t: فَدَنَا مِنْهُ وَمَسَكَ يَدَهُ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ الَّذِي كُنْتَ تُنْشِدُ الشِّعْرَ فَخَافَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَقَالَ لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا مُقَدَّمَ الْقَوْمِ مَا هُوَ أَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-danā minhu wa-masaka yadahu wa-qāla lahu anta alladhī kunta tunshidu al-shiʿra fa-khāfa ʿalā nafsihi wa-qāla lā wa-allāhi yā muqaddama al-qawmi mā huwa anā
sentences.l: So he drew near him and seized his hand and said to him: You are the one who were reciting the poetry. And he feared for himself and said: No, by God, O foremost-of-the-people, it is not I.
sentences.i: He went up to him, took him by the hand, and said: You are the one who was reciting the verses! The stoker feared for himself and said: No, by God, O captain of the people, it was not I.
sentences.n: مسك for مَسَكَ (rather than Classical أَمْسَكَ) is ordinary Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ لَا أَتْرُكُكَ حَتَّى تَدُلَّنِي عَلَى مَنْ كَانَ يُنْشِدُ الشِّعْرَ لِأَنِّي أَخَافُ مِنْ سَيِّدَتِي إِذَا أَنَا رَجَعْتُ لَهَا بِغَيْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu lā atrukuka ḥattā tadullanī ʿalā man kāna yunshidu al-shiʿra li-annī akhāfu min sayyidatī idhā anā rajaʿtu lahā bi-ghayrihi
sentences.l: And the servant said to him: I will not leave you until you guide me to the one who was reciting the poetry, for I fear my mistress if I return to her with other than him.
sentences.i: The servant said: I will not let you go until you show me who was reciting the verses, for I am afraid of my mistress if I go back to her with anyone else.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَقَّادُ كَلَامَ الْخَادِمِ خَافَ عَلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَبَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَقَالَ لِلْخَادِمِ وَاللَّهِ مَا هُوَ أَنَا وَلَا أَعْرِفُهُ وَإِنَّمَا سَمِعْتُ إِنْسَانًا عَابِرَ سَبِيلٍ يُنْشِدُ فَلَا تَدْخُلْ فِي خَطِيئَتِي فَإِنِّي غَرِيبٌ وَجِئْتُ مِنْ بِلَادِ الْقُدْسِ وَالْخَلِيلِ مَعَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-waqqādu kalāma al-khādimi khāfa ʿalā ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-bakā bukāʾan shadīdan wa-qāla li-al-khādimi wa-allāhi mā huwa anā wa-lā aʿrifuhu wa-innamā samiʿtu insānan ʿābira sabīlin yunshidu fa-lā tadkhul fī khaṭīʾatī fa-innī gharībun wa-jiʾtu min bilādi al-quds wa-al-khalīli maʿakum
sentences.l: And when the stoker heard the servant’s speech, he feared for Ḍawʾ al-Makān and wept a violent weeping, and said to the servant: By God, it is not I, and I do not know him; I only heard a person, a passer-of-the-way, reciting. So do not enter into my fault, for I am a stranger, and I came from the lands of Jerusalem and Hebron with you.
sentences.i: When the stoker heard the servant’s words, he feared for Ḍawʾ al-Makān and wept bitterly, and said to the servant: By God, it was not I, and I do not know him; I only heard a passer-by reciting. Do not make me answer for his fault, for I am a stranger who came with you all from the land of Jerusalem and Hebron.
sentences.n: فلا تدخل في خطيئتي is loosely worded; read as “do not drag me into guilt”. The last words, “with you”, refer to the company with whom he travelled.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ قُمْ أَنْتَ مَعِي وَاحْكِ لِسَيِّدَتِي بِفَمِكَ فَإِنِّي مَارَأَيْتُ أَحَدًا مُسْتَيْقِظًا غَيْرَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu qum anta maʿī wa-ḥki li-sayyidatī bi-famika fa-innī mā raʾaytu aḥadan mustayqiẓan ghayraka
sentences.l: And the servant said to him: Rise, you, with me, and tell my mistress with your mouth, for I have not seen anyone wakeful but you.
sentences.i: The servant said: Get up and come with me, and tell my mistress with your own mouth, for I have seen no one awake but you.
sentences.n: The print has مستقيظا, a misprint for مستيقظا, corrected here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ اَمَا جِئْتَ وَرَأَيْتَنِي فِي هَذَا الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ قَاعِدٌ وَعَرَفْتَ مَكَانِي وَمَا أَحَدٌ يَقْدِرُ أَنْ يَنْفَكَّ عَنْ مَوْضِعِهِ إِلَّا أَمْسَكَتْهُ الْحُرَّاسُ فَامْضِ أَنْتَ إِلَى مَكَانِكَ وَإِنْ عُدْتَ تَسْمَعْ أَحَدًا مِنْ هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ يُنْشِدُ شَيْأً مِنَ الشِّعْرِ سَوَاءٌ كَانَ بَعِيدًا أَوْ قَرِيبًا فَيَكُونُ أَنَا أَوْ أَحَدٌ أَعْرِفُهُ وَلَا تَعْرِفُهُ إِلَّا مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu amā jiʾta wa-raʾaytanī fī hādhā al-mawḍiʿi alladhī anā fīhi qāʿidun wa-ʿarafta makānī wa-mā aḥadun yaqdiru an yanfakka ʿan mawḍiʿihi illā amsakat-hu al-ḥurrāsu fa-miḍi anta ilā makānika wa-in ʿudta tasmaʿ aḥadan min hādhihi al-sāʿati yunshidu shayʾan mina al-shiʿri sawāʾun kāna baʿīdan aw qarīban fa-yakūnu anā aw aḥadun aʿrifuhu wa-lā taʿrifuhu illā minnī
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: Did you not come and see me in this place in which I am sitting, and you know my position; and no one can part from his place but the guards seize him. So go, you, to your place; and if you return, you will hear anyone from this hour reciting anything of poetry, whether far or near, it will be I or someone I know; and you will know him only from me.
sentences.i: The stoker said: Did you not come and see me in this place where I sit? You know where I am, and no one can leave his post without the guards seizing him. Go back to your own place. And if from this hour you hear anyone reciting any verse at all, far or near, then it will be I, or someone I know, and you will learn of him only from me.
sentences.n: The print’s اَمَا carries a fatḥa on the alif, kept here. The last sentences are loosely built; the sense is that the stoker will report any reciter himself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَبَّلَ رَأْسَ الْخَادِمِ وَأَخَذَ بِخَاطِرِهِ فَتَرَكَهُ الْخَادِمُ وَدَارَ دَوْرَةً وَجَاءَ فَاسْتَتَرَ وَوَقَفَ مِنْ وَرَاءِ الْوَقَّادِ وَخَافَ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ إِلَى سَيِّدَتِهِ بِلَا فَائِدَةٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qabbala raʾsa al-khādimi wa-akhadha bi-khāṭirihi fa-tarakahu al-khādimu wa-dāra dawratan wa-jāʾa fa-istatara wa-waqafa min warāʾi al-waqqādi wa-khāfa an yarjiʿa ilā sayyidatihi bi-lā fāʾidatin
sentences.l: Then he kissed the servant’s head and took hold of his heart, and the servant left him, and went a turn, and came, and hid himself, and stood behind the stoker, and feared to return to his mistress without profit.
sentences.i: Then he kissed the servant’s head and won him over, and the servant left him. But he went a little way round, came back, hid himself and stood behind the stoker, afraid to return to his mistress empty-handed.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ الْوَقَّادُ إِلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَنَبَّهَهُ وَقَالَ لَهُ قُمِ اجْلِسْ حَتَّى أَحْكِىَ لَكَ مَا جَرَى فَقَامَ فَحَكَى لَهُ مَا وَقَعَ فَقَالَ لَهُ دَعْنِي فَإِنِّي مَا عُدْتُ أُفَكِّرُ وَلَا أُبَالِي بِأَحَدٍ فَإِنَّ بِلَادِي قَرِيبَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma al-waqqādu ilā ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-nabbahahu wa-qāla lahu qumi ijlis ḥattā aḥkiya laka mā jarā fa-qāma fa-ḥakā lahu mā waqaʿa fa-qāla lahu daʿnī fa-innī mā ʿudtu ufakkiru wa-lā ubālī bi-aḥadin fa-inna bilādī qarībatun
sentences.l: Then the stoker rose to Ḍawʾ al-Makān and woke him and said to him: Rise, sit, that I may tell you what has happened. So he rose, and he told him what had occurred. And he said to him: Leave me, for I no longer think, nor care about anyone, for my country is near.
sentences.i: Then the stoker went to Ḍawʾ al-Makān and woke him, saying: Get up and sit, and I will tell you what has happened. He got up, and the stoker told him all that had occurred. Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: Leave me be, for I no longer think of it, nor care about anyone; my own country is near.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَقَّادُ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ أَنْتَ مُطَاوِعٌ نَفْسَكَ وَالشَّيْطَانَ وَأَنْتَ لَا تَخَافُ مِنْ أَحَدٍ وَأَنَا خَائِفٌ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَى نَفْسِي فَبِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ مَا بَقِيتَ تَتَكَلَّمُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الشِّعْرِ حَتَّى تَدْخُلَ بَلَدَكَ فَإِنِّي مَا كُنْتُ أَظُنُّكَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-waqqādu li-ḍawʾi al-makāni li-ayyi shayʾin anta muṭāwiʿun nafsaka wa-al-shayṭāna wa-anta lā takhāfu min aḥadin wa-anā khāʾifun ʿalayka wa-ʿalā nafsī fa-bi-allāhi ʿalayka mā baqīta tatakallamu bi-shayʾin mina al-shiʿri ḥattā tadkhula baladaka fa-innī mā kuntu aẓunnuka ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati
sentences.l: And the stoker said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: For what thing are you obeying your self and the devil, when you fear no one, and I am afraid for you and for myself? By God upon you, do not go on speaking with anything of poetry until you enter your country; for I did not think you to be in this state.
sentences.i: The stoker said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: Why do you yield to your own impulse and to the devil, when you fear no one while I am afraid for you and for myself? I beg you by God, say no more verse until you reach your country; I never thought you would be in this state.
sentences.n: ما بقيت تتكلم is an emphatic prohibition (“do not go on speaking”), a Middle Arabic use of ما with the perfect.

sentences.t: أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ هَذِهِ السِّتَّ زَوْجَةُ الْحَاجِبِ تُرِيدُ زَجْرَكَ لِأَنَّكَ أَتْلَفْتَهَا وَكَأَنَّهَا مَرِيضَةٌ أَوْ سَهَرٌ إِنَّةُ مِنْ تَعَبِ السَّفَرِ وَبُعْدِ الْمَسَافَةِ وَهَذِهِ ثَانِي مَرَّةٍ وَهِيَ تُرْسِلُ الْخَادِمَ يُفَتِّشُ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: amā ʿalimta anna hādhihi al-sitta zawjatu al-ḥājibi turīdu zajraka li-annaka atlaftahā wa-ka-annahā marīḍatun aw saharun innatu min taʿabi al-safari wa-buʿdi al-masāfati wa-hādhihi thānī marratin wa-hiya tursilu al-khādima yufattishu ʿalayka
sentences.l: Did you not know that this lady, the wife of the chamberlain, wants your zaḥr, because you ‘atlaq’-ed her, and as if she were ill, or sleeplessness — it is from the fatigue of travel and the distance of the road; and this is the second time, and she is sending the servant searching for you.
sentences.i: Do you not know that this lady, the chamberlain’s wife, means to rebuke you because you have distressed her? She seems ill, or sleepless from the fatigue of the journey and the long road, and this is the second time she has sent the servant to search for you.
sentences.n: The print has زحرك, a misprint for زجرك, corrected here. The print has اتلقتها, a misprint for أتلفتها, corrected here. انة is printed with ة for ه (إنه “it is”).

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَلْتَفِتْ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ إِلَى كَلَامِ الْوَقَّادِ بَلْ صَاحَ ثَالِثًا وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yaltafit ḍawʾu al-makāni ilā kalāmi al-waqqādi bal ṣāḥa thālithan wa-anshada yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: But Ḍawʾ al-Makān paid no heed to the stoker’s speech; rather he cried out a third time and recited, saying these verses:
sentences.i: But Ḍawʾ al-Makān paid no attention to the stoker’s words; he cried out a third time and recited these verses:

sentences.t:
تَرَكْتُ كُلَّ لَائِمْ * مَلَامُهُ اَقْلَقَنِي
يَعْذِلُنِي وَمَا دَرَى * بِاَنَّهُ حَرَّضَنِي
قَالَ الْوُشَاةُ قَدْ سَلَا * قُلْتُ لِحُبِّ الْوَطَنِ
قَالُوْا فَمَا اَحْسَنَهُ * قُلْتُ فَمَا اَعْشَقَنِي
قَالُوْا فَمَا اَعَزَّهُ * قُلْتُ فَمَا اَذَلَّنِي
هَيْهَاتَ اَنْ اَتْرُكَهُ * لَوْ جُرِعْتُ كَاسَ الشَّجَنِ
وَمَا اَطَعْتُ لَائِمًا * فِيْ حُبِّهِ يَعْذِلُنِي
sentences.tr:
taraktu kulla lāʾimin * malāmuhu aqlaqanī
yaʿdhilunī wa-mā darā * bi-annahu ḥarraḍanī
qāla al-wushātu qad salā * qultu li-ḥubbi al-waṭani
qālū fa-mā aḥsanahu * qultu fa-mā aʿshaqanī
qālū fa-mā aʿazzahu * qultu fa-mā adhallanī
hayhāta an atrukahu * law juriʿtu kāsa al-shajani
wa-mā aṭaʿtu lāʾimān * fī ḥubbihi yaʿdhilunī
sentences.l:
I have left every blamer * his blame has unsettled me
He scolds me, and does not know * that he has only spurred me on
The slanderers said: He has forgotten! * I said: For love of the homeland
They said: How fair it is! * I said: How I long for it
They said: How dear it is! * I said: How abased I am
Far be it that I leave it * though I were made to swallow the cup of grief
And I have not obeyed a blamer * in his love of it, who scolds me
sentences.i:
I have left every critic behind; his blame has only unsettled me.
He scolds me and does not know that he has spurred me on.
The slanderers said: He has forgotten! I said: For love of the homeland.
They said: How fair it is! I said: How I long for it.
They said: How dear it is! I said: How abased I am.
Far be it from me to leave it, though I be made to drink the cup of grief;
nor have I obeyed any critic who scolds me for loving it.
sentences.n: The edition points this poem and its pointing is kept as printed. A few readings are loose: the second line of the second couplet reads “he has spurred me on” (حرّضني); the sixth couplet’s جرعت is printed without shadda.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ كَانَ الْخَادِمُ يَسْمَعُهُ وَهُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ فَمَا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ وَانْتَهَى إِلَّا وَالْخَادِمُ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ فَلَمَّا رَآهُ الْوَقَّادُ فَرَّ وَوَقَفَ بَعِيدًا يَنْظُرُ مَا يَقَعُ بَيْنَهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi kāna al-khādimu yasmaʿuhu wa-huwa mustakhfin fa-mā faragha min shiʿrihi wa-intahā illā wa-al-khādimu ʿalā raʾsihi fa-lammā raʾāhu al-waqqādu farra wa-waqafa baʿīdan yanẓuru mā yaqaʿu baynahumā
sentences.l: And when he had finished his poetry — the servant had been listening to him, while hiding — he had not finished his poetry and ended but that the servant was at his head. And when the stoker saw him, he fled and stood far off, watching what would happen between them.
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses — the servant had been listening in hiding all the while — he had scarcely finished and stopped before the servant was standing over him. When the stoker saw this, he fled and stood at a distance, watching what would pass between them.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا سَيِّدِي فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ فَقَالَ الْخَادِمُ يَا سَيِّدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu al-salāmu ʿalaykum yā sayyidī fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-ʿalaykumu al-salāmu wa-raḥmatu allāhi wa-barakātuhu fa-qāla al-khādimu yā sayyidī
sentences.l: And the servant said to him: Peace be upon you, O my master. And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: And upon you be peace, and the mercy of God and His blessings. And the servant said: O my master —
sentences.i: The servant said to him: Peace be upon you, my lord. Ḍawʾ al-Makān replied: And upon you be peace, and the mercy of God and His blessings. Then the servant said: My lord —

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night.
